style: dark burnished steel and polished brass game art, engraved metal, cool neon rim light, painted illustration, high contrast, clean silhouette
notes: One art style, repeated word for word at the head of every prompt (rule F.1c). Every mechanical sprite declares its orientation in words (rule C.8), and the rotationally symmetric ones say so explicitly so nothing is mirrored by accident. Only sprite_pulse_trail, sprite_target_gate and icon_back are directional: the first two point DOWN because the code places them on the rim and rotates them to aim at the core, and icon_back points LEFT. The sprites the code TINTS at runtime - sprite_notch_marker, sprite_target_gate, sprite_key_token, sprite_section_pip, sprite_pulse_trail, sprite_spark_fx - are drawn in pale neutral silver-white with value contrast only, because a tint multiplies: brass art tinted brass turns to mud, and the same token has to read as crimson, amber, violet or teal depending on which key is live. Everything else carries its own colour and is drawn untinted. The three gear rings are HOLLOW so the rings inside them stay visible. sprite_vault_plate carries a 48px nine-slice border in its .meta, so its prompt asks for a uniform riveted rim and a flat centre that survives stretching. Sprites are drawn on whatever backdrop the model likes because the pipeline cuts the background away (rule F.1b). No prompt contains the app name and no sprite carries lettering of any kind (hard rule 1).
